note: Written by the daily Claude review (NEWS-UPDATING.md). items: per-story summary, category, importance and sector scores, keyed by the story id in news.json. extra: stories Claude found itself. brief: today's key points.

points.text: Merck and Moderna's personalised mRNA cancer vaccine cut the risk of relapse or death by 42% in phase 3 melanoma, the first clear late-stage win for the modality, though a weaker secondary measure knocked both shares.
FDA approved GSK and Ionis' Hibsago (bepirovirsen), the first antisense drug for chronic hepatitis B and a step towards a functional cure.
US Treasury's draft COINS Act rules would sharply restrict American investment in Chinese biotech while exempting licensing deals, reshaping how pharma sources assets from China.
EQT agreed to take molecular diagnostics company Qiagen private for €10.8 billion, the year's largest life science tools deal.
The UK committed £100 million to an AI Biosecurity Lab, working with frontier AI developers to monitor biological threats.
Amgen's Imdelltra with Imfinzi cut the risk of death by 58% in first-line extensive-stage small cell lung cancer, published in NEJM alongside ESMO.
